subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a stable hotfix/repacked release for the v2026.6.11 reply-session initialization package-parity regression, or instead mark 2026.6.11 affected until the next stable train?
rationale: The source-side fix is present on current main, but the unresolved user impact is in the latest published stable package; deciding the release path requires maintainer release authority rather than another source-only fix PR.

options.title: Ship stable package parity hotfix
options.body: Publish a new stable package from a source tree with the reentrant writer and reply-init metadata fixes, then validate the npm tarball and close this issue with release proof.

options.title: Document 2026.6.11 as affected
options.body: If a hotfix is not acceptable, keep this issue open and point users away from v2026.6.11 until the next stable release ships the fixed dist.

options.title: Wait for next stable train
options.body: Leave latest stable affected until the next scheduled stable release, accepting the ongoing message-loss/session-state risk during the wait.

recommendation.title: Ship stable package parity hotfix
recommendation.body: Publish a new stable package from a source tree with the reentrant writer and reply-init metadata fixes, then validate the npm tarball and close this issue with release proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current latest stable tag is a release-stabilization commit authored by Vincent Koc, making this the best available release-parity routing signal.
